calls: Realistic total: US $59.1K over the 12 days (11.3% TACoS) vs $76.2K actually spent in BFCM 2025 (8.2%). Canada C$19.0K at 11.4% (BFCM 2025: C$31.1K). The account runs at 20% TACoS today across all ad types (14.1% before BFCM 2025), so the deal-period TACoS starts higher.

Demand re-based on Nov 3 to current, event-free selling: each product's last-14-day pace (Oct 19 - Nov 1) x its own BFCM 2025 lift, and, where the product sold in both years, its BFCM 2025 units x how it is running against the same 14 days last year. The Oct 28 read used paces that included the Oct 7-8 Prime event and late-September deals, about twice today's pace on the Bamboo sheets. Plan units: US Decolure Bamboo 4 Pc 1,911 (was 3,501); US Decolure Bamboo 6 Pc 1,340 (was 2,345); US Decolure Satin 4 Pc 2,790 (was 3,019); CA Decolure Bamboo 4 Pc 597 (was 699); CA Decolure Bamboo 6 Pc 736 (was 949). Budget moves from the Nov 2 plan's US $88.3K / C$25.5K to $59.1K / C$19.0K.

SB, SB video and SD are tracked per product (Ad types by product tab): each product's TACoS now, break-even and cap include all four ad types, and its budget splits by its own mix. US plan: SP $47.2K, SB $5.1K, SB video $5.9K, SD $0.9K. Canada is 98% SP.

Aligned with the growth plan: each product's TACoS sits inside its growth-plan band (scaled for the deal), never above break-even. Raised to the growth floor: US Sleephoria Cooling Fitted, US Sleephoria Bamboo 6 Pc, CA Decolure Bamboo 6 Pc. Held at the cap: US Sleep Sanctuary Satin 4 Pc, US CooLinens Pillowcases, US Decolure Satin Fitted, US Decolure Silk Pillowcase, US Sleephoria Cooling Pillowcase, CA Decolure Satin 4 Pc, CA Decolure Satin 6 Pc.

Over the cap today, bring down before Nov 19 (TACoS now vs cap). US: CooLinens Pillowcases (53% vs 15%), Sleephoria Cooling Pillowcase (52% vs 16%), Sleep Sanctuary Satin 4 Pc (21% vs 12%), Decolure Cooling 4 Pc (31% vs 23%), Decolure Silk Pillowcase (32% vs 25%), Decolure Satin Fitted (18% vs 12%), Sleephoria Cooling 4 Pc (30% vs 25%), Decolure Satin 6 Pc (15% vs 12%), Decolure Chair Cover (21% vs 18%), Decolure Satin 4 Pc (13% vs 12%). CA: Decolure Satin 4 Pc (20% vs 12%), Decolure Satin 6 Pc (17% vs 12%), Decolure Satin Fitted (16% vs 12%), Sleep Sanctuary Satin 4 Pc (14% vs 12%).

Decisions for Joseph: CooLinens Pillowcases is a Launch product (band 25%-40%) but at the $15.10 deal break-even only allows 15%, so it is capped there. CooLinens Cooling Sheets has no deal: the plan holds today's ~$740 a day (33% TACoS, inside its Launch band).
No ads beyond brand defence on Sleephoria Quilt Set (break-even -1.6%), Decolure Linen Curtains (break-even -26.8%): at the deal price they lose money or keep almost nothing per unit before ads.

History check (2025 vs 2026 check tab): in BFCM 2025 we spent 1.6x (US) / 2.3x (CA) more per day than in the same 14 days before; sales rose 2.9x / 3.2x and TACoS fell from 14.6% to 8.2% (US). Doing the same from today gives US $72.8K / C$19.7K (check A). The plan is 19% below that in the US and 4% below in Canada, because it expects sales to jump 2.5x (US) / 3.0x (CA) vs 2.9x / 3.2x in 2025, and holds each product inside its TACoS cap. Suggest: approve the plan as the base budget and check A as the ceiling; the agent releases the extra only while each product stays under its TACoS cap on actual sales.

Where we stand vs last year (same 14 days): US sales -32%, traffic -34%, ad spend -4%, so TACoS is 20.5% vs 14.6%; clicks are 27% cheaper and conversion is unchanged (6.7%). Canada: sales -46%, traffic -56%, spend -37%. After BFCM 2025 spend stayed about 1.5x for two weeks at 11% TACoS (Dec 1 - 15 is outside this budget).

Year over year, same 14 days (Oct 19 - Nov 1): US ad spend is down only 4% ($54.7K to $52.3K), but the mix changed. Products sold both years cut SP by $21.8K and added $1.8K of SB / SB video / SD; new products (CooLinens, Sleephoria Cooling Fitted, Bamboo Fitted) added $18.2K. Like-for-like sales fell 48% ($351K to $183K) with traffic down 34% and conversion steady, so like-for-like TACoS rose from 15.3% to 18.5%. For BFCM, the plan for products that ran in 2025 is $47.4K vs $75.6K spent on them last year; the rest ($11.7K) is new products.

Every number is an estimate from the last 14 days of sales and spend by product and ad type, each product's BFCM 2025 lift and the Oct 27 deal prices. Amazon's deal prices can still change until Nov 13; the plan is re-run if they do.
